hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions About AfriNuts Export
hero.subtitle: Organic Cashews, Farm OS Technology, and Ethical Investment
hero.lead: From Farm OS technology to organic certification timelines — find clear answers about how we grow, track, and export cashews from Odienné, Côte d'Ivoire.
hero.description: Get clear answers about our tech-enabled cashew farm in Odienné, Ivory Coast. Learn about Farm OS traceability, organic practices, processing plans, community impact, and how to partner with us.

stillQuestions.title: Didn't find your answer
stillQuestions.content: Ask us anything about our farm, products, or investment opportunities.

questions.question: What is AfriNuts Export?
questions.answer: AfriNuts Export SARL is a tech-enabled cashew farm and future processing company based in Odienné, Côte d'Ivoire. Incorporated in June 2026 under OHADA law (RCCM: CI-ABJ-03-2026-B12-04223, IDU: CI-2026-0066959 J). We grow organic cashews on 35 hectares, operate a live supplier intelligence network via Farm OS, and reinvest 10% of profits into community development.

questions.question: What is Farm OS?
questions.answer: Farm OS is our custom-built farm operating system — an offline-first Android application with cloud synchronization. It tracks every block, every tree, every expense, every harvest, and every supplier. Buyers get block-level traceability. Investors get real-time dashboards. Partners can license it. It is live today, not a roadmap item.

questions.question: Where is your farm located?
questions.answer: Our 70-hectare estate is in Odienné, northwestern Côte d'Ivoire: 35 hectares under cashew cultivation, 10 hectares reserved for the processing center, and 25 hectares for a separate community development project. Every farm block is GPS-mapped in Farm OS.

questions.question: What products do you offer?
questions.answer: Phase One focuses on domestic raw cashew nut trading. Future phases will produce premium processed kernels (W320, W240, W180), CNSL by-product, and value-added products like roasted cashews, cashew butter, and cashew milk.

questions.question: How do you differ from other cashew exporters?
questions.answer: Three differences: (1) We build the supply chain before the factory — trading and supplier intelligence come first. (2) Farm OS provides block-level traceability that most West African exporters cannot match. (3) We reinvest 10% of profits into community development and operate on Shariah-compliant principles.

questions.question: How does Phase One generate returns?
questions.answer: Phase One trades raw cashew nuts domestically. The base case projects $14,520 profit per truck ($30,000 capital deployed, 42 metric tons), or roughly $43,560 across three trucks. Equity investors receive 10% of net trading profit as it is realized — no deferral to 2033. Mudarabah partners receive 20% of actual realized profit per cycle, with AfriNuts retaining 80%.

questions.question: When do equity investors see a return?
questions.answer: Equity investors begin participating in Phase One trading profits immediately. As each trading cycle closes and profit is realized, 10% is distributed to equity holders — proportionate to their ownership stake. There is no deferral. The 2033 dividend timeline applies only to Phase Two processing profits, which is the long-term upside.

questions.question: How is profit distributed between equity and Mudarabah investors?
questions.answer: Equity investors: 10% of net Phase One trading profit, distributed as each cycle closes. Mudarabah partners: 20% of actual realized profit per cycle, with AfriNuts retaining 80%. In Phase Two (2033+), the dividend policy shifts to 50% of net profits distributed, 50% reinvested for expansion.

questions.question: Why is the Mudarabah share 20% while equity is 10%?
questions.answer: Equity investors receive 10% because they own 10% of the company and share in all future value — trading profits, processing dividends, and equity appreciation. Mudarabah partners receive 20% of actual realized trading profit per cycle but have no permanent equity stake and no claim on future company value. The two structures are different: one is ownership, the other is a defined transaction-based partnership.

questions.question: What happens to the remaining trading profit?
questions.answer: AfriNuts retains its share to fund operations, supplier development, certification readiness, and future growth. The retained capital recycles into each trading cycle. Full distribution terms are in the Shareholders' Agreement (equity) and Mudarabah contracts, available after NDA.

questions.question: How do you grow your cashews?
questions.answer: We plant 100 trees per hectare across 35 individually tracked blocks. Our Farm OS logs planting dates, survival rates, and maintenance activities per block — not per farm. We also maintain a nursery reserve of 500 seedlings for replacement.

questions.question: When is your harvest season?
questions.answer: Our first trees were planted in 2026. First small harvest expected 2029, with peak production by 2031. Every harvest is logged in Farm OS by block, date, and volume — buyers receive this data with their shipment.

questions.question: Are your cashews organic?
questions.answer: While not yet certified organic, we use sustainable and chemical-minimal farming methods that align with agroecological practices. We plan to pursue organic certification as part of our ESG goals.

questions.question: What sustainability practices do you follow?
questions.answer: We use rainfed agriculture to conserve water and avoid the need for irrigation in Phase 1. We also employ firebreaks to prevent wildfires, practice agroforestry where possible, and maintain natural buffers to preserve biodiversity.

questions.question: How do you manage water and waste?
questions.answer: Our farm relies on natural rainfall, and we avoid chemical runoff. As we expand, we will develop water-efficient systems and composting solutions to maintain soil health and reduce waste.

questions.question: What is your approach to ESG?
questions.answer: AfriNuts is committed to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles. This includes reinvesting in local infrastructure, promoting inclusive hiring, and ensuring transparent governance aligned with ethical values.

questions.question: How is the farm aligned with Islamic investment principles?
questions.answer: We operate under a no-riba (no interest) policy and prioritize partnerships that reflect shared risk and profit. Our investor model is based on ethical financing, community benefit, and long-term sustainability.

questions.question: Is there interest (riba) involved in your funding model?
questions.answer: No. We do not charge or pay interest. Our investors receive a share of the net profit (e.g., 25%) based on performance, not fixed returns. This aligns with Islamic financial ethics.

questions.question: How do you reinvest profits into the community?
questions.answer: We reinvest 10% of our net profits into local community initiatives. Examples include: drilling water wells, supporting local madrasas (Islamic schools), and contributing to mosque maintenance. This is our commitment to sadaqah jariyah — ongoing charity that benefits generations.

questions.question: When will the processing center be operational?
questions.answer: The cashew processing center is planned for construction starting in 2028, pending land title finalization and Phase Two investment. Our target is commercial operations by 2031. We will share updates as milestones are reached.

questions.question: What capacity will the processing center have?
questions.answer: Phase Two begins with a pilot facility processing 1,000–2,000 MT of raw cashew nuts per year, producing 250–500 MT of premium kernels. Long-term expansion targets 70,000–100,000 MT/year as we scale.

questions.question: What makes your center eco-friendly?
questions.answer: Our center will integrate solar power, water-efficient systems, and ethical labor practices. We aim to build a model agro-industrial site that minimizes carbon emissions and supports the circular economy.

questions.question: Will it serve the local community?
questions.answer: Yes. Beyond cashew processing, the center will provide employment, skill training, and community development. It is part of our broader vision to establish Odienné as a hub for ethical agriculture.

questions.question: How do you ensure the quality of your cashews?
questions.answer: Quality control starts in the field. Farm OS tracks moisture content, nut count, and defect rates per batch. Every batch is linked to its farmer, source type, and quality metrics. When you receive a shipment, you receive the data — not just the nuts.

questions.question: Are your products traceable?
questions.answer: Yes — and we mean that differently than most suppliers. Farm OS provides block-level traceability: GPS coordinates, harvest date, processing batch, and quality metrics. Enter your batch ID on our Trace page and see the full journey yourself. No login required.

questions.question: Do you track supplier sustainability?
questions.answer: Yes. Every batch is verified for no child labor, firebreak protection, and sustainable harvesting — with timestamp and verifier ID. This is per-batch verification, not a company-level promise.

questions.question: Can you trace a batch to a specific farmer?
questions.answer: Yes. Every batch links to its farmer — name, photo, years of experience, location, and personal bio. Source types are tracked: Owned Farm, Cooperative, Independent, or Regional Supplier. The same traceability standard applies across the entire network.

questions.question: What logistics options do you offer?
questions.answer: We ship from the Port of Abidjan — one of West Africa's most efficient deep-water ports. Current lead times: 4-6 weeks to Europe, 6-8 weeks to North America, 3-4 weeks to Middle East. We offer FOB Abidjan and can arrange CIF for qualified buyers. Every shipment includes Farm OS traceability documentation.

questions.question: What is your minimum order quantity?
questions.answer: Our standard MOQ is 1 metric ton (approximately 20 jute bags) for raw cashew nuts. For processed kernels and specialty products, MOQs vary — contact us for details.

questions.question: Do you offer bulk pricing?
questions.answer: Yes, we offer tiered pricing based on order volume. Please contact our sales team for detailed pricing information.

questions.question: What certifications do you have?
questions.answer: We are pursuing Organic (target 2029), Fair Trade (target 2030), ISO 22000 (target 2030), Halal (target 2030), and Rainforest Alliance (target 2029). Our farm is already transitioning to organic practices since planting in 2026. Documentation is available upon request.

questions.question: Can I request samples before ordering?
questions.answer: Yes. Sample boxes are available for qualified buyers. Contact our sales team to request a sample with full traceability documentation.

questions.question: What exactly am I investing in?
questions.answer: A $350,000 Phase One raise for 10% equity in AfriNuts Export SARL, at a $3.5M post-money valuation (minimum investment $50,000). This phase funds domestic raw cashew trading operations and the supplier intelligence network — it does not fund the processing plant, which is a later phase.

questions.question: What is the difference between the equity and Mudarabah options?
questions.answer: Two Shariah-compliant paths: (1) equity ownership — 10% of the company at $3.5M post-money, with 10% of net Phase One trading profit distributed as realized, plus future dividends from Phase Two. (2) Mudarabah trading partnership — 20% of actual realized profit per trading cycle, no permanent equity stake. Both are reviewed for Shariah compliance before any funds are accepted.

questions.question: What is the expected return on investment?
questions.answer: Equity investors participate in Phase One trading profits (10% of net profit) as cycles close, and receive dividends from Phase Two processing (target 2033+). Mudarabah partners receive 20% of actual realized trading profit per cycle. Full projections are available under NDA.

questions.question: When do investors receive dividends?
questions.answer: Equity investors receive 10% of net Phase One trading profit as it is realized — not deferred. From 2033 onward, once commercial processing is established, the dividend policy shifts to 50% of net profits distributed, 50% reinvested for Phase Two expansion. Mudarabah partners receive 20% of profit per trading cycle throughout.

questions.question: How can I become a partner?
questions.answer: We welcome partnerships with distributors, retailers, and complementary businesses. Please contact our partnership team to discuss opportunities.

questions.question: Do you offer white-label options?
questions.answer: Yes, we offer white-label packaging and private label options for qualified partners with sufficient order volumes.

questions.question: What support do you provide to partners?
questions.answer: We provide marketing materials, product training, and joint promotional opportunities to our partners to ensure mutual success.

questions.question: What partnership models do you offer?
questions.answer: We offer four models: (1) Outgrower Cooperative — expand our farmer network, (2) White-Label/Co-Packing — we process under your brand, (3) Farm OS Licensing — deploy our platform on your farm, (4) Joint Venture Processing — build processing centers together. Visit our Partners page for details.

questions.question: Is Farm OS available for licensing?
questions.answer: Yes. We offer Farm OS licensing for large-scale farms, agribusinesses, and government programs. The platform is crop-agnostic — currently built for cashew but adaptable to cocoa, shea, coffee, and other crops. Contact us to discuss deployment.

questions.question: Can I visit the farm before partnering?
questions.answer: Absolutely. We encourage serious partners to visit our 35-hectare farm in Odienné and see Farm OS in action. There is no substitute for seeing the operation firsthand. Visits are arranged on request.

questions.question: Do you offer white-label or private label options?
questions.answer: Yes. We offer white-label processing and packaging for qualified partners with sufficient volume. Your brand, our Farm OS traceability, and our certified supply chain.

questions.question: What is the minimum commitment for a partnership?
questions.answer: We design pilot projects with small scope and clear metrics before scaling. Minimum volumes depend on the partnership model. Contact our partnership team to discuss your specific needs.

questions.question: Who leads AfriNuts Export?
questions.answer: AfriNuts is led by Hamza Sangare (CEO) — a software engineer who built Farm OS himself — alongside a team with expertise in finance, agriculture, technology, and community development. Our founder's dual background in tech and farming is what makes our operating model possible.

questions.question: How is governance handled?
questions.answer: Our governance is transparent and participatory, with oversight from both local stakeholders and external advisors to ensure accountability.

questions.question: How is the project financed?
questions.answer: The project is financed through a mix of equity investment, ethical financing, and reinvested profits. We avoid debt with interest (riba) to align with our values.

questions.question: Do you offer financial reports?
questions.answer: Yes. We provide regular financial updates and transparent reporting to all stakeholders and investors.
